newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian government to replace arrested rail chief.
newsitem.headline: Italian government to replace arrested rail chief.

text.p: The Italian government plans to replace arrested state railways chief Lorenzo Necci, who is being held in custody in a corruption probe, Transport Minister Claudio Burlando said on Tuesday.
He told the transport committee of the Senate, the upper house of parliament, that the government favoured appointing someone from outside the company, Ferrovie dello Stato.
"The government has decided to nominate a new managing director quickly and the decision is to find a solution outside the company," Burlando said.
He said the change would not affect rail projects, which include the modernisation of certain routes and the development of a multi-billion-dollar high-speed rail system.
"We must not confuse the acts of one person, who will answer to the magistrates, with the development programmes for our country," the minister said.

Necci was arrested on September 15 on suspicion of offences which include corruption, abuse of office, false accounting and fraud. He is being held in pre-trial detention in a jail in the northwest port of La Spezia, where the probe is based.
Since his arrest, his duties have been handled by rail chairman Giorgio Crisci and the board.
